question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment.

Despite the difficulties, Sarah started her business with great energy and hard work, and performed remarkably well in the industry.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. hit the ground running.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to hit the ground running" means to start an activity or task with great energy, enthusiasm and success right from the beginning. It perfectly replaces "started her business with great energy and hard work". (पूरे जोश और सफलता के साथ शुरुआत करना)

◦ Example: The new manager hit the ground running and doubled sales in a month.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "hit the hay" — to go to bed / sleep.

• Option 3 "spilled the beans" — to reveal a secret.

• Option 4 "let sleeping dogs lie" — to avoid interfering in a situation that could cause trouble.

NOTE

• The idiom comes from the image of someone leaping off and running immediately. Similar idioms of energetic starts: "off to a flying start", "up and running".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The mother told the child to erase the extra dots from the given graph.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Create.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Erase" means to remove or rub out (something written or drawn). Its antonym is "create", which means to make or produce something. (मिटाना का विलोम — बनाना)

◦ Example: You can erase a pencil mark, but only an artist can create a masterpiece.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "Delete" and Option 4 "Efface" are synonyms of erase.

• Option 2 "Shatter" (to break into pieces) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of erase: delete, efface, remove, obliterate, wipe out.

• Antonyms: create, produce, make, form, generate.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

She oftenly goes / shopping with / her friends / on Saturdays.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. She oftenly goes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Often" is already an adverb — there is no word "oftenly". So "oftenly" is wrong; the correct form is "often".

◦ Correct: She often goes shopping with her friends on Saturdays.

• As an adverb of frequency, "often" is placed before the main verb ("often goes").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "shopping with", "her friends" and "on Saturdays" are all correct.

NOTE

• Some adverbs do NOT take "-ly": often, seldom, fast, hard, well. Writing "oftenly", "fastly" or "hardly" (in the sense of "in a hard way") is a common error. Note: "hardly" exists but means "scarcely".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.

No sooner had she enter her apartment than she found a bouquet of flowers on her table.
option_2: No sooner did she entered her apartment than
option_3: No sooner did she enter her apartment than
option_4: No sooner has she enter her apartment than
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. No sooner did she enter her apartment than.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "No sooner ... than" is used for two actions happening in quick succession. When it begins a sentence, it causes inversion — the auxiliary comes before the subject. With the simple past, we use "did + subject + base verb": "No sooner did she enter ... than ...".

◦ Correct: No sooner did she enter her apartment than she found a bouquet of flowers.

• The original "had she enter" is wrong because after "had" we need the past participle "entered", not "enter".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "did she entered" wrongly uses "entered" after "did" (it should be the base form "enter").

• Option 4 "has she enter" uses the wrong auxiliary/tense.

NOTE

• "No sooner ... than" (not "then"); "Hardly/Scarcely ... when/before". Both take inversion at the start: "No sooner had I reached than it rained" OR "No sooner did I reach than it rained".

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in future continuous tense form.

Shall I meet you soon?
option_1: Shall I have met you soon?
option_2: Shall I be meeting you soon?
option_4: Will I be meeting you soon?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Shall I be meeting you soon?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The future continuous tense is formed as shall/will + be + verb-ing. Keeping the same subject "I" and object "you" as in the original, the correct form is "Shall I be meeting you soon?"

◦ Future continuous: shall/will + be + V-ing (be meeting).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Shall I have met you soon?" is future perfect (shall have + V3).

• Options 3 and 4 change the subject/object ("we", "I ... you") but Option 4 also fits the form; however, the exact conversion preserving "I meet you" is Option 2 with "Shall I".

NOTE

• Future tense forms: Simple future (will meet), Future continuous (will be meeting), Future perfect (will have met), Future perfect continuous (will have been meeting). Traditionally, "shall" is used with I/we.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

The rules of behaviour which guide one in a formal situation
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Protocol.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Protocol" means the accepted rules of correct or formal behaviour, especially in official or diplomatic situations. (शिष्टाचार / प्रोटोकॉल)

◦ Example: The visiting dignitary was received according to strict protocol.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Affidavit" — a written statement made on oath.

• Option 3 "Bargain" — an agreement / a good deal in buying and selling.

• Option 4 "Impropriety" — improper or unacceptable behaviour (the opposite idea).

NOTE

• "Protocol" also means the original draft of a treaty, or a set of rules in computing/science. In common usage it refers to etiquette and formal procedure.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Cautios.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Cautios" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Cautious", meaning careful to avoid danger or mistakes. (सतर्क / सावधान)

◦ Example: Be cautious while crossing the busy road.

• Spelling key: CAU + TIOUS — the ending is "-tious" (like ambitious, nutritious).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Anxious", "Curious" and "Bashful" (shy) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Adjectives ending in "-ous": cautious, anxious, curious, courageous, gracious, ambitious. Related forms: caution (noun), cautiously (adverb).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The company ran about of stock due to unexpectedly high demand for the product.
option_1: ran out of stock due to
option_2: ran around of stock due to
option_3: ran across of stock due to
option_4: ran on of stock due to
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. ran out of stock due to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrasal verb is "run out of", meaning to use up the entire supply of something / to have none left. Hence "the company ran out of stock". (समाप्त हो जाना / स्टॉक खत्म होना)

◦ Correct: The company ran out of stock due to unexpectedly high demand.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "ran about", "ran around" and "ran on" do not convey the meaning of exhausting the stock.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "run": run out of (exhaust supply), run into (meet by chance / collide), run across (find by chance), run over (hit with a vehicle), run down (criticise / lose power).

question:
Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given sentence.

Enthusiasm is one of those vital elements that transforms an indvdual and his failures into victories and success.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Indivdual.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Indivdual" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Individual", meaning a single, separate person. (व्यक्ति)

◦ Example: Every individual has the right to education.

• Spelling key: IN + DI + VI + DU + AL — note the "vidu" (there must be a "u" after "vid").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Success", "Victories" and "Failures" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related words: individual, individually, individuality, individualism. A common error is dropping the "i" or "u" — remember IN-DI-VI-DU-AL.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Disclaimer on products in the markets saves manufacturer from unusual results on usage.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Clause.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "disclaimer" is a statement or clause that denies responsibility or limits liability — for example, warning that a company is not responsible for misuse of a product. Its closest meaning here is "clause". (अस्वीकरण खंड / शर्त)

◦ Example: The website has a disclaimer stating it is not liable for external links.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Guarantee" (a promise of quality), Option 2 "Approval" (official acceptance) and Option 4 "Acceptance" all carry the opposite sense of endorsing responsibility, not denying it.

NOTE

• A disclaimer typically limits or rejects legal responsibility. Related legal terms: clause, provision, caveat, waiver.

question:
Select the most appropriate degree to fill in the blank.

Doctors should never be __________ than others when patients come for their treatment.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. less caring.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" requires the comparative degree. The context ("should never be ___ than others") calls for a negative comparison — doctors should not be less caring than others. (कम देखभाल करने वाले)

◦ Correct: Doctors should never be less caring than others ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "more caring" is grammatically comparative but reverses the intended meaning (doctors SHOULD be more caring, so "should never be more caring" is illogical).

• Options 1 "least caring" and 3 "most caring" are superlatives, which cannot be used with "than".

NOTE

• Comparative degree is used with "than": more caring / less caring than. Superlatives (most/least caring) take "the" and compare three or more, not "than".

question:
Select the option that rectifies the underlined spelling error.

The panel submited the findings to the ministry.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. submitted.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "submitted", the past tense of "submit". When a word ends in a single vowel + a single consonant and the stress is on the last syllable (sub-MIT), the final consonant is doubled before "-ed" → submit + t + ed = submitted. (प्रस्तुत किया)

◦ Example: She submitted her assignment on time.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 3 ("submittad", "submittd", "sumitted") are all misspellings.

NOTE

• Consonant-doubling rule (stress on last syllable): submit → submitted, prefer → preferred, occur → occurred, refer → referred, permit → permitted.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Clear the decks
option_3: To remove unnecessary things for further work
option_4: Prepare for an event or course of action by dealing with anything that might hinder progress
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Prepare for an event or course of action by dealing with anything that might hinder progress.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to clear the decks" means to prepare for action by removing all obstacles or finishing other tasks that might get in the way. (आगे के कार्य के लिए तैयारी करना / बाधाएँ हटाना)

◦ Example: Before the exams, she cleared the decks by finishing all her pending work.

• It comes from the naval practice of clearing the ship's decks before a battle.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 3 is close but incomplete; the idiom specifically means preparing for a coming task by dealing with anything that might hinder it, not merely removing things.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of preparation: "gear up", "set the stage", "get one's ducks in a row".

question:
Identify the error in the following sentence.

The zoo is under the street from the temple.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. under.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition "under" (meaning below) is wrong for describing two places on opposite sides of a street. The correct preposition is "across" — "The zoo is across the street from the temple." (के आर-पार / सामने)

◦ Correct: The zoo is across the street from the temple.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "zoo", "temple" and "from" are all correct. "Across ... from" is a fixed way of saying "on the opposite side".

NOTE

• Prepositions of place: across (on the other side), under/below (beneath), beside/next to (at the side), between (in the middle of two), among (in the middle of many).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

The order will be operational from 1st of November.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. effective.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Operational", when describing a rule or order, means in force, working or effective. Its closest synonym is "effective" (coming into effect / operative). (प्रभावी / लागू)

◦ Example: The new traffic rules will be operational/effective from Monday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "considered" (thought about), Option 2 "provoked" (incited) are unrelated.

• Option 3 "scrapped" (cancelled/abolished) is an antonym in this context.

NOTE

• Synonyms of operational (in force): effective, functional, operative, in effect, working. Antonyms: inoperative, non-functional, scrapped.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four parts. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error.

A student becomes / dearer to the teachers / via participating and actively working / towards the glory of the school.
option_4: towards the glory of the school
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. dearer to the teachers.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The comparative adjective "dearer" requires a "than" comparison, which is absent here. The sentence simply describes a quality, so the positive degree "dear" should be used — "becomes dear to the teachers".

◦ Correct: A student becomes dear to the teachers via participating and actively working ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "A student becomes", "via participating and actively working" and "towards the glory of the school" are acceptable.

NOTE

• Use the comparative ("dearer") only with an explicit or implied "than" (dearer than gold). Without comparison, use the positive degree ("dear").

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

He was appointed as the Manager.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Dismissed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Appointed" means assigned a job or position to someone. Its antonym is "dismissed", meaning removed from a job or position. (नियुक्त किया का विलोम — बर्खास्त किया)

◦ Example: He was appointed in January but dismissed in June for misconduct.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "Assigned" is a synonym of appointed.

• Option 2 "Disordered" (in a mess) and Option 4 "Disappointed" (let down) are unrelated (do not be misled by the "dis-" prefix).

NOTE

• Synonyms of appoint: nominate, designate, assign, engage.

• Antonyms: dismiss, remove, sack, discharge, terminate.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

Her team played exceptionally more well in the competition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. well.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Well" is the adverb here, and it is already modified by "exceptionally". We do not use "more" with "well" (its comparative form is "better", not "more well").

◦ Correct: Her team played exceptionally well in the competition.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "most well" and Option 4 "more well" are both wrong; the degrees of "well" are well – better – best (irregular).

NOTE

• Irregular comparison: well/good – better – best; badly/bad – worse – worst; much/many – more – most; little – less – least. Never say "more well" or "more better".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I have never __________ this kind of pain before surgery.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. experienced.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Experienced" means felt or underwent (something). It fits the context of feeling pain and correctly forms the present perfect ("have never experienced"). (अनुभव किया)

◦ Example: I have never experienced such cold weather before.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "practised" (did repeatedly to improve), Option 3 "trained" (taught a skill) and Option 4 "dedicated" (devoted) do not collocate with "pain".

NOTE

• "Experience" as a verb means to feel/undergo; as a noun it means knowledge gained over time. Collocation: experience pain / joy / difficulty / a problem.

question:
Select the word that has the same meaning (SYNONYM) as the underlined word in the given sentence.

The doctor made a tentative diagnosis as he did not have the reports of her blood tests.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. provisional.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Tentative" means not certain or fixed; done as a trial and subject to change. Its closest synonym is "provisional" (temporary, arranged for the present but likely to change). (अनंतिम / अस्थायी)

◦ Example: They made a tentative/provisional booking that could be changed later.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "tedious" (boring), Option 3 "hazardous" (dangerous) and Option 4 "obsolete" (out of date) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of tentative: provisional, temporary, unconfirmed, speculative, trial.

• Antonyms: definite, final, confirmed, conclusive.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Indian villages showcase the country's rich culture and customs. Most Indians live in villages, (1)_______ agriculture, modest living and close-knit communities are the norms. Villagers wake up to roosters crowing and farm (2)_______ day. Farming is the main employment, and generations labour (3)_____ the same land. Traditions, communal events and a slower pace (4)______ village life from metropolitan life. Villagers' togetherness and shared duty make it part of India's identity, (5)_____ the lack of contemporary conveniences.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. where.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The relative adverb "where" is used to refer to a place (villages) — "villages, where agriculture, modest living ... are the norms." (जहाँ)

◦ Correct: Most Indians live in villages, where agriculture ... are the norms.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "what" and Option 3 "which" would need a different structure; "which" refers to things but cannot smoothly introduce this place-clause here.

• Option 4 "when" refers to time, not place.

NOTE

• Relative words: where (place), when (time), which/that (things), who/whom (people), whose (possession).

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Indian villages showcase the country's rich culture and customs. Most Indians live in villages, (1)_______ agriculture, modest living and close-knit communities are the norms. Villagers wake up to roosters crowing and farm (2)_______ day. Farming is the main employment, and generations labour (3)_____ the same land. Traditions, communal events and a slower pace (4)______ village life from metropolitan life. Villagers' togetherness and shared duty make it part of India's identity, (5)_____ the lack of contemporary conveniences.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. all.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "All day" means throughout the whole day. It fits the context of villagers farming for the entire day. (पूरे दिन)

◦ Correct: Villagers wake up to roosters crowing and farm all day.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "towards", Option 3 "before" and Option 4 "after" do not correctly express the sense of "for the whole day".

NOTE

• Common time expressions: all day, all night, all week, all year (round). "All day" = from morning to evening.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Indian villages showcase the country's rich culture and customs. Most Indians live in villages, (1)_______ agriculture, modest living and close-knit communities are the norms. Villagers wake up to roosters crowing and farm (2)_______ day. Farming is the main employment, and generations labour (3)_____ the same land. Traditions, communal events and a slower pace (4)______ village life from metropolitan life. Villagers' togetherness and shared duty make it part of India's identity, (5)_____ the lack of contemporary conveniences.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. on.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition "on" is used with "land" — "generations labour on the same land", meaning they work upon that land. (भूमि पर काम करना)

◦ Correct: ... generations labour on the same land.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "labour with/at/in the same land" are not the correct collocations; we work on the land / on a farm.

NOTE

• Preposition + place collocations: work on the land/a farm/a field, work in an office/a factory, work at a desk/a company.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Indian villages showcase the country's rich culture and customs. Most Indians live in villages, (1)_______ agriculture, modest living and close-knit communities are the norms. Villagers wake up to roosters crowing and farm (2)_______ day. Farming is the main employment, and generations labour (3)_____ the same land. Traditions, communal events and a slower pace (4)______ village life from metropolitan life. Villagers' togetherness and shared duty make it part of India's identity, (5)_____ the lack of contemporary conveniences.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. distinguish.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Distinguish" means to mark or recognise the difference between two things. The sentence contrasts village life with metropolitan (city) life, so "traditions ... and a slower pace distinguish village life from metropolitan life". It takes the structure "distinguish X from Y". (अंतर करना / भिन्न करना)

◦ Correct: ... a slower pace distinguish village life from metropolitan life.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "compare" (find similarities/differences — usually "compare with/to"), Option 2 "balance" and Option 4 "equate" (to treat as equal) do not fit the "X from Y" structure that shows a difference.

NOTE

• "Distinguish X from Y" = to tell X apart from Y. Synonyms: differentiate, discriminate, tell apart. Note the preposition "from".

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Indian villages showcase the country's rich culture and customs. Most Indians live in villages, (1)_______ agriculture, modest living and close-knit communities are the norms. Villagers wake up to roosters crowing and farm (2)_______ day. Farming is the main employment, and generations labour (3)_____ the same land. Traditions, communal events and a slower pace (4)______ village life from metropolitan life. Villagers' togetherness and shared duty make it part of India's identity, (5)_____ the lack of contemporary conveniences.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. despite.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Despite" means in spite of; regardless of and is directly followed by a noun/noun phrase (no "of"). It shows contrast — village togetherness makes it part of India's identity despite the lack of modern conveniences. (के बावजूद)

◦ Correct: ... make it part of India's identity, despite the lack of contemporary conveniences.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "in spite" is incomplete — it must be "in spite of".

• Option 2 "beside" (next to) and Option 3 "instead of" (in place of) do not fit the contrast.

NOTE

• "Despite + noun" and "In spite of + noun" mean the same (do NOT write "despite of"). For a clause, use "although / though / even though".

question: Which dynasty defeated the Kanva dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Satavahana Dynasty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Satavahana dynasty (founded by Simuka) defeated/overthrew the Kanva dynasty around 28 BCE, establishing their rule in the Deccan region. (सातवाहन वंश ने कण्व वंश को पराजित किया)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Sequence of Magadha dynasties: Haryanka → Shishunaga → Nanda → Maurya → Shunga → Kanva → Satavahana.

• The Kanva dynasty (founded by Vasudeva Kanva) had itself replaced the Shunga dynasty.

• The most famous Satavahana ruler was Gautamiputra Satakarni.

NOTE

• The Satavahanas issued lead and potin coins, promoted trade, and their inscriptions are an important source of ancient Indian history (e.g., the Nasik Prashasti).

question: Which of the following best represents the Revenue Deficit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Revenue Expenditure – Revenue Receipts.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure − Revenue Receipts. It arises when the government's revenue expenditure exceeds its revenue receipts, meaning it cannot meet even its day-to-day running expenses from its regular income. (राजस्व घाटा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure − Total Receipts (excluding borrowings) = the total borrowing requirement of the government.

• Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit − Interest Payments.

• Effective Revenue Deficit = Revenue Deficit − Grants for creation of capital assets.

NOTE

• Revenue receipts (tax + non-tax) do not create a liability or reduce assets; a revenue deficit is considered undesirable as it implies borrowing for consumption, not investment.

question: The non-metallic mineral mica is used in which of the following industries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Electrical industry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The non-metallic mineral "mica" is widely used in the electrical and electronics industry because it is an excellent insulator — it has high dielectric strength, low power loss and resistance to heat. (अभ्रक — विद्युत उद्योग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• India is one of the largest producers of mica; major deposits are in Jharkhand, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan (the Koderma belt of Jharkhand is famous).

• Mica is also used in making capacitors, insulators and electronic components.

NOTE

• Non-metallic minerals include mica, limestone, gypsum, dolomite and manganese (metallic). Mica's key property for the electrical industry is its insulating (dielectric) capacity.

question: Which virus is responsible for causing AIDS?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome) is caused by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV). HIV attacks and weakens the body's immune system, specifically the CD4 (helper T) cells, making the body vulnerable to infections. (एड्स — एचआईवी वायरस)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• HIV is a retrovirus and mainly spreads through unprotected sexual contact, contaminated blood/needles, and from an infected mother to child.

• 1 December is observed as World AIDS Day.

NOTE

• HPV causes cervical cancer and warts; HSV causes herpes; Influenza virus causes flu. This is a sensitive health topic; the focus here is purely the factual virus-disease association tested in exams.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India emphasises the participation of workers in the management of industries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 43A.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 43A of the Constitution directs the State to take steps to secure the participation of workers in the management of undertakings/industries. (अनुच्छेद 43A — उद्योगों के प्रबंधन में श्रमिकों की भागीदारी)

• It was added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Article 43A is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), Part IV of the Constitution.

• Related labour DPSPs: Article 39 (adequate means of livelihood, equal pay), Article 41 (right to work), Article 43 (living wage), Article 43B (promotion of cooperatives).

NOTE

• DPSPs are non-justiciable (not enforceable in court) but are "fundamental in the governance of the country" (Article 37). They aim at establishing a welfare state.

question: Which of the following two properties of metals are exploited to prepare very thin sheets of silver to decorate sweets?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Malleability and lustre.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The thin silver sheets (chandi ka varq) used to decorate sweets exploit two metallic properties:

◦ Malleability — the ability of a metal to be beaten/hammered into thin sheets.

◦ Lustre — the shine of the metal, which gives the sweets a decorative, attractive appearance. (आघातवर्धनीयता एवं चमक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Ductility is the ability to be drawn into thin wires (e.g., copper, gold).

• Sonorous means metals produce a ringing sound when struck (used in bells).

NOTE

• Key physical properties of metals: malleability, ductility, lustre, sonorousness, high melting point, and good conductivity of heat and electricity. Gold and silver are the most malleable and ductile metals.

question: What is the quorum of the Lok Sabha at the time of the Presidential address, which is held at the opening of each session of the Lok Sabha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is One-tenth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The quorum (minimum number of members required to conduct business) of the Lok Sabha (and Rajya Sabha) is one-tenth (1/10) of the total number of members of the House, as laid down in Article 100(3) of the Constitution. (गणपूर्ति — कुल सदस्यों का 1/10)

• For the Lok Sabha (545 members), the quorum is therefore about 55 members.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• If there is no quorum, it is the duty of the Speaker/Chairperson to adjourn the House or suspend the meeting until there is a quorum.

• The President addresses both Houses together at the commencement of the first session after each general election and at the start of the first session of each year (Article 87).

NOTE

• Articles on Parliament: 79 (constitution of Parliament), 80 (Rajya Sabha), 81 (Lok Sabha), 100 (voting and quorum).

question: As of July 2023, who was the Member of Parliament from the parliamentary constituency of Varanasi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narendra Modi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of July 2023, Narendra Modi, the Prime Minister of India, was the Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha) from the Varanasi parliamentary constituency in Uttar Pradesh. (वाराणसी — नरेंद्र मोदी)

• He was first elected from Varanasi in 2014 and re-elected in 2019 and 2024.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Varanasi (Kashi/Banaras) is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, situated on the banks of the Ganga, and a major religious and cultural centre.

• Rajnath Singh represents Lucknow; Smriti Irani represented Amethi (2019).

NOTE

• The Lok Sabha is directly elected by the people; a candidate must be at least 25 years old to contest a Lok Sabha seat.

question: The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College in Aligarh was founded by __________.
option_4: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Kalam'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/Kalam.ttf') format('truetype');} </style>Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sir Syed Ahmed Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) College at Aligarh was founded in 1875 by Sir Syed Ahmed Khan, a social reformer and educationist, to promote modern, Western-style education among Indian Muslims. (सर सैयद अहमद खान — एमएओ कॉलेज)

• This later grew into the Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) in 1920.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sir Syed Ahmed Khan started the Aligarh Movement for the social and educational upliftment of Muslims.

• He also wrote "Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind" (The Causes of the Indian Revolt of 1857).

NOTE

• Other important educational institutions: Banaras Hindu University (BHU) by Madan Mohan Malaviya (1916), Jamia Millia Islamia (1920).

question: Panch Mahal, a palace in Fatehpur Sikri, was built by the Mughal Emperor __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Akbar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Panch Mahal, a five-storeyed palace in Fatehpur Sikri, was built by the Mughal Emperor Akbar. It is an open, column-based pavilion, each storey smaller than the one below, used for relaxation and enjoying the breeze. (पंच महल — अकबर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri (near Agra) and made it his capital for a time; it is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

• Other structures at Fatehpur Sikri: the Buland Darwaza (built to commemorate the Gujarat victory), the Jama Masjid, Diwan-i-Khas, Diwan-i-Aam and the tomb of Salim Chishti.

NOTE

• Akbar (1556–1605) followed a policy of religious tolerance (Sulh-i-Kul), introduced Din-i-Ilahi, and abolished the Jizya (tax on non-Muslims).

question: The Jhaveri Sisters are known for keeping alive the temple tradition of which of the following classical dances of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipuri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Jhaveri Sisters (Nayana, Ranjana, Suverna and Darshana Jhaveri) are renowned for reviving and keeping alive the Manipuri classical dance tradition. (मणिपुरी नृत्य — झावेरी सिस्टर्स)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Manipuri dance, from Manipur, is known for its gentle, graceful and fluid movements, and themes based on Radha–Krishna (Raslila) and Vaishnavism.

• The dancers wear a distinctive stiff, decorated skirt called the "Kumil".

NOTE

• Classical dances and their states: Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kathak (North India), Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha).

question: The historical novel, 'Train to Pakistan' was written by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khushwant Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Train to Pakistan" (1956) is a famous historical novel written by Khushwant Singh. It vividly depicts the horrors and human tragedy of the Partition of India in 1947 through the fictional village of Mano Majra. (ट्रेन टू पाकिस्तान — खुशवंत सिंह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Khushwant Singh was a noted author, journalist and Padma Vibhushan awardee; his other works include "Delhi: A Novel" and "The Company of Women".

• Other Partition literature: "Tamas" (Bhisham Sahni), "Ice-Candy-Man / Cracking India" (Bapsi Sidhwa).

NOTE

• Author–book pairs for SSC: The God of Small Things (Arundhati Roy), The Great Indian Novel (Shashi Tharoor), The Discovery of India (Jawaharlal Nehru).

question: The Indravati National Park is located in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indravati National Park is located in the Bijapur district of Chhattisgarh, on the banks of the Indravati River. It is one of the finest and best-known wildlife reserves of the state and is also a Tiger Reserve. (इंद्रावती राष्ट्रीय उद्यान — छत्तीसगढ़)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Indravati National Park is famous for the wild buffalo and the rare Barasingha (swamp deer), along with tigers, leopards and gaur.

• Other national parks in Chhattisgarh: Kanger Valley and Guru Ghasidas (Sanjay) National Park.

NOTE

• The Indravati River is a tributary of the Godavari. India has over 100 national parks; the first was Jim Corbett (1936, Uttarakhand).

question: Emani Sankara Sastry and Doraiswamy Iyengar are both associated with which musical instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Veena.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Emani Sankara Sastry and Mysore Doraiswamy Iyengar were both eminent maestros of the Veena, a classical stringed instrument of India. (वीणा वादक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Veena (Saraswati Veena) is one of the oldest Indian instruments, closely associated with Carnatic music and the goddess Saraswati.

• It is a plucked string instrument known for its rich, resonant tone.

NOTE

• Instrument–artist pairs: Veena (S. Balachander, Doraiswamy Iyengar), Flute (Hariprasad Chaurasia), Sitar (Ravi Shankar), Sarod (Amjad Ali Khan), Shehnai (Bismillah Khan), Ghatam (Vikku Vinayakram).

question: According to the census of India 2011, which of the following states is least urbanised?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census 2011, among the given options Himachal Pradesh was the least urbanised state, with only about 10% of its population living in urban areas. (हिमाचल प्रदेश — न्यूनतम शहरीकृत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Himachal Pradesh had the lowest urbanisation among all Indian states (about 10%), followed by Bihar (about 11%).

• The most urbanised state was Goa (about 62%); among UTs, Delhi and Chandigarh are almost fully urban.

NOTE

• India's overall urban population in 2011 was about 31.16%. Urbanisation is measured as the percentage of population living in towns/cities.

question: Consider the following pairs (Work – Writer): 1. Rajtaringini – Kalhan   2. Gita Govinda – Chandbardai   3. Vikramarjuna-Vijaya – Pampa. Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 3.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pair 1 is correct: "Rajatarangini" (a chronicle of the kings of Kashmir) was written by Kalhana.

• Pair 3 is correct: "Vikramarjuna Vijaya" (also called Pampa Bharata) was written by Pampa, the great Kannada poet (Adikavi).

• Pair 2 is WRONG: "Gita Govinda" was written by Jayadeva, not Chandbardai. (Chand Bardai wrote the "Prithviraj Raso".)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2 (pairs 1 and 3).

Additional Information

• Rajatarangini (12th century) is considered one of the earliest works of historical writing in India.

• Pampa is called the "Adikavi" (first poet) of Kannada literature.

NOTE

• Famous work–author pairs: Prithviraj Raso (Chand Bardai), Gita Govinda (Jayadeva), Harshacharita/Kadambari (Banabhatta), Mudrarakshasa (Vishakhadatta).

question: The navigable portion of Barak River in India is the 121 km stretch between Lakhipur and Bhanga, which was declared as _______ in the year 2016.
solution_text:
The correct answer is NW-16.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 121 km navigable stretch of the Barak River between Lakhipur and Bhanga was declared as National Waterway 16 (NW-16) in 2016. (बराक नदी — राष्ट्रीय जलमार्ग-16)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Barak River flows through Assam and is important for the Barak Valley region.

• Major National Waterways: NW-1 (Ganga: Prayagraj–Haldia), NW-2 (Brahmaputra: Dhubri–Sadiya), NW-3 (West Coast Canal, Kerala).

NOTE

• National Waterways are declared under the National Waterways Act, 2016, and managed by the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) for cheap and eco-friendly water transport.

question: Against which of the following were 'Swadeshi' and 'Boycott' used as the means of protest and struggle, for the first time in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Partition of Bengal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The methods of "Swadeshi" (using Indian-made goods) and "Boycott" (of British goods and institutions) were first adopted on a large scale during the anti-Partition of Bengal agitation (1905), launched against Lord Curzon's partition of Bengal. (बंगाल विभाजन — स्वदेशी एवं बहिष्कार आंदोलन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Swadeshi Movement promoted Indian industries, national education and the use of khadi.

• The Partition of Bengal (1905) was finally annulled in 1911.

NOTE

• Later, Mahatma Gandhi used Swadeshi and Boycott in the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920). Leaders of the Swadeshi movement included Bipin Chandra Pal, Lala Lajpat Rai and Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Lal-Bal-Pal).

question: A hockey ground is rectangular in shape, measuring 91.4 m in length and _______ in width.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 55 m.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A standard field hockey ground is rectangular, measuring 91.4 metres (100 yards) in length and 55 metres (60 yards) in width. (हॉकी मैदान — 91.4 मी × 55 मी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Hockey is often regarded as India's national game (unofficially); India won 8 Olympic gold medals in hockey (six in a row from 1928 to 1956).

• Major Dhyan Chand is called the "Wizard of Hockey"; his birthday (29 August) is National Sports Day.

NOTE

• Playing-area dimensions for SSC: Hockey (91.4 m × 55 m), Football (length 100–110 m), Cricket pitch (22 yards ≈ 20.12 m).

question:
The National Population Register was created under the provisions of _______ and _______.

a. the Citizenship Act, 1965   b. the Citizenship Rules, 2004   c. the Citizenship Act, 1955   d. the Citizenship Rules, 2003
solution_text:
The correct answer is c; d (the Citizenship Act, 1955 and the Citizenship Rules, 2003).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Population Register (NPR) was created under the provisions of the Citizenship Act, 1955 and the Citizenship (Registration of Citizens and Issue of National Identity Cards) Rules, 2003. (एनपीआर — नागरिकता अधिनियम 1955 एवं नियम 2003)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The NPR is a register of the usual residents of the country (a person who has resided in a local area for at least 6 months or intends to stay for the next 6 months).

• It is prepared at the local, sub-district, district, state and national levels, under the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (Ministry of Home Affairs).

NOTE

• The NPR is different from the NRC (National Register of Citizens) — the NPR records residents, while the NRC is meant to record citizens.

question: In May 2023, the Supreme Court interpreted which article related to the governance structure of Delhi, which outlines the principles of federalism, participatory democracy and collective responsibility?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 239AA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In May 2023, the Supreme Court interpreted Article 239AA, which deals with the special governance structure of the National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi. The Court ruled on the division of powers between the elected Delhi government and the Lieutenant Governor, upholding principles of federalism, participatory democracy and collective responsibility. (अनुच्छेद 239AA — दिल्ली की शासन संरचना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Article 239AA (inserted by the 69th Amendment, 1991) gave Delhi a Legislative Assembly and a Council of Ministers, but kept land, police and public order with the Centre.

• The 2023 verdict held that the Delhi government has control over services (except the three reserved subjects), though this was later modified by an ordinance/law.

NOTE

• Article 243B relates to Panchayats; Article 323A to Administrative Tribunals; Article 226 to the writ jurisdiction of High Courts.

question: Nishagandhi festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Nishagandhi Dance and Music Festival is celebrated in Kerala, at the Nishagandhi open-air auditorium in Thiruvananthapuram. It showcases India's classical dance and music forms. (निशागंधी महोत्सव — केरल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The festival is organised by the Kerala Tourism Department and features leading classical artists from across India.

• Other festivals of Kerala: Onam (harvest festival), Thrissur Pooram (temple festival) and Vishu.

NOTE

• Kerala, "God's Own Country", is famous for its backwaters, Ayurveda, and the classical arts Kathakali and Mohiniyattam.

question: Which Bharatanatyam dancer is the recipient of one of India's top civilian award, the Padma Vibhushan 1977?
solution_text:
The correct answer is T Balasaraswati.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tanjore Balasaraswati (T. Balasaraswati), the legendary Bharatanatyam dancer, was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 1977. She was renowned worldwide for her expressive abhinaya and played a major role in popularising Bharatanatyam globally. (टी. बालासरस्वती — पद्म विभूषण 1977)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• She had earlier received the Padma Bhushan (1957) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, one of the oldest and based on the Natya Shastra.

NOTE

• Kelucharan Mohapatra was an Odissi maestro; Yamini Krishnamurthy and Mallika Sarabhai are noted Bharatanatyam/Kuchipudi dancers of a later generation.

question: Where was the inaugural season of Ultimate Kho-Kho League held in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pune.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The inaugural season of the Ultimate Kho-Kho (UKK) League was held in 2022 in Pune, Maharashtra. Odisha Juggernauts won the first title. (अल्टीमेट खो-खो लीग — 2022, पुणे)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kho-Kho is a traditional Indian tag/pursuit sport played between two teams; it, along with Kabaddi, is a popular indigenous game.

• The Ultimate Kho-Kho League is a franchise-based professional league aimed at popularising the sport.

NOTE

• India hosted the first Kho-Kho World Cup in 2025 (New Delhi), with the Indian men's and women's teams winning the titles.

question:
Which of the following options correctly matches Column-A (Cell organelles) with Column-B (Function)?

i. Cell membrane   ii. Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum   iii. Golgi apparatus   iv. Ribosomes  |  a. Protein synthesis  b. Important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids  c. Synthesis of lipid  d. Transport of the molecules
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-d, ii-c, iii-b, iv-a.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct matching of cell organelles with their functions is:

◦ i. Cell membrane → d. Transport of the molecules (it regulates the movement of substances in and out of the cell — it is "selectively permeable").

◦ ii. Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum → c. Synthesis of lipid (the smooth ER makes lipids and steroids).

◦ iii. Golgi apparatus → b. Important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids (it modifies, packages and dispatches materials).

◦ iv. Ribosomes → a. Protein synthesis (ribosomes are the site of protein manufacture).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1 (i-d, ii-c, iii-b, iv-a).

Additional Information

• The Rough ER (with ribosomes) helps in protein synthesis and transport; the Golgi apparatus is called the "post office of the cell".

• Mitochondria are the "powerhouse of the cell"; lysosomes are the "suicidal bags".

NOTE

• The cell is the structural and functional unit of life. Ribosomes are the only organelle also found in prokaryotes (bacteria), which lack membrane-bound organelles.
